title: Microscopic Modeling of the Charge-Density-Waves in the Rare-Earth Tritellurides
authors: Sijia Zhao, Julian May-Mann, Ian R. Fisher, Steven A. Kivelson
abstract: Despite being arguably the simplest and best characterized quasi-2D charge-density-wave (CDW) systems, the rare-earth tritellurides ($R$Te$_3$) continue to yield surprising experimental results, including recent evidence suggestive of mirror-symmetry breaking associated with the onset of CDW order. Motivated by this, we consider a 2D electron-phonon model for a single Te square-net plane, which we analyze using mean-field theory. For an appropriate region of parameter space, we find a finite-temperature continuous transition from the normal state to a unidirectional CDW state with an ordering vector matching that observed experimentally. At lower temperatures, we find a second translation-symmetry-breaking transition, similar to what occurs in $R$Te$_3$ compounds with heavier rare-earth elements. In certain parameter regimes, we also find an intervening mirror-symmetry-breaking transition occurring between the two transitions described above. These results reveal an intrinsic susceptibility to mirror-symmetry breaking in the unidirectional CDW phase, which is relevant to understanding recent experiments on the $R$Te$_3$ compounds.
summary: This theoretical study models CDW formation in rare-earth tritellurides using a 2D electron-phonon Hamiltonian. By analyzing the free energy and collective excitations, the authors predict a sequence of symmetry-breaking transitions, crucially demonstrating that the CDW state is highly susceptible to mirror-symmetry breaking. This provides a microscopic framework to explain complex experimental observations in these materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the origin of surprising experimental observations in rare-earth tritellurides ($	ext{RTe}_3$), specifically focusing on evidence suggesting mirror-symmetry breaking associated with the onset of Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) order.
main_result: The model predicts a sequence of transitions ($T_{c1} 	o T^* 	o T_{c2}$) and shows that the CDW phase is intrinsically susceptible to mirror-symmetry breaking, which can be amplified by weak perturbations.
method: The study employs mean-field theory, Ginzburg-Landau functional expansions, and real-space minimization techniques applied to a 2D electron-phonon model.
model_or_system: The system is the quasi-2D rare-earth tritelluride ($	ext{RTe}_3$), modeled using a 2D electron-phonon Hamiltonian ($\hat{H} = \hat{H}_e + \hat{H}_{e-	ext{ph}} + \hat{H}_{	ext{ph}}$) for a single Te square-net plane.
key_observables: CDW order parameter, phonon spectrum (especially low-lying modes), mirror susceptibility ($\chi_M$), and the temperature evolution of symmetry breaking.
important_parameters: Coupling ratios ($g_{\perp}/g_{\parallel}$), stiffness ratios ($K_2/K_1$), and temperature ($T_{c1}, T^*, T_{c2}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field theory, the adiabatic limit (neglecting quantum phonon fluctuations), and uses commensurate approximations for the ordering vector for numerical tractability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing CDW instability dependence on parameters, and temperature evolution plots detailing the sequence of transitions and the softening of specific phonon modes (Mode 3 and Mode 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the basic 2D electron-phonon model, analyzing the high-temperature CDW onset via mean-field theory, and then refining the analysis by examining the low-temperature sequence of symmetry-breaking transitions ($T^*, T_{c2}$) using advanced free energy minimization and mode analysis.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of symmetry breaking (mirror and glide) in a strongly correlated electronic state driven by lattice coupling provides a rich theoretical playground for understanding emergent symmetries in condensed matter systems.
